Fit a survival model at every landmark

Source: R/fit_landmark.R
fit_landmark.Rd

fit_landmark() fits one independent regression model per landmark of a landmark_tbl: a Cox proportional hazards model (survival::coxph()) or a Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards model (survival::finegray() followed by a weighted survival::coxph()). The outcome is built internally from .time and .status, so formula only lists the covariates.

Usage

fit_landmark(
  data,
  formula,
  model = c("cox", "finegray"),
  cause = 1,
  progress = getOption("tidylandmark.progress", interactive())
)

Arguments

data

A landmark_tbl, as returned by landmark_data() or add_landmark_covariates().

formula

A one-sided formula of covariates, e.g. ~ age + sex + bili. Any right-hand side that survival::coxph() accepts can be used, including factors, interactions, transformations (log(bili)), splines (splines::ns(age, 3)) and strata(). Leave out Surv(). The formula can't use ., reserved columns (.time, .status, ...), tt() or cluster().

model

"cox" (default) or "finegray".

cause

The event of interest: one of the event codes of the status given to landmark_data() (e.g. 1), or, if status was a factor, one of its event levels (e.g. "relapse"). Default 1.

progress

Show a progress bar while fitting? Defaults to the tidylandmark.progress option, or interactive() if it is unset.

Value

A landmark_fit object: a list with

  • data: the landmark_tbl that was fitted.

  • models: one fitted survival::coxph() object per landmark, named by landmark (NULL where no model was fitted). For Fine-Gray models this is the weighted fit to the expanded data.

  • model_info: a tibble with one row per landmark: .landmark, .model, .cause, n_eligible (rows at risk), n_model (complete cases used), n_event and n_competing (target and competing events in the model sample), .fit_status ("ok", "warning", "unestimable" or "failed") and .message (NA when "ok").

  • coefficients: a tibble with one row per landmark and model term: .landmark, term, estimate and std.error (log scale) and origin ("baseline", "locf", "lme", or e.g. "baseline:lme" for an interaction).

  • warnings: a tibble of the warnings captured from each fit.

  • config: the formula, model, cause and related settings.

Use tidy() for a results table and print() or summary() for an overview.

Details

Models

With model = "cox", each landmark gets coxph(Surv(.time, .status == cause) ~ <formula>) with Efron's method for ties. If the status coding has a single event type, this is an ordinary Cox model. If it has other event types, they are treated as censored at their event time, so the model estimates cause-specific hazard ratios; the .model column then reads "cause-specific cox".

With model = "finegray", survival::finegray() expands each landmark's data with time-dependent censoring weights for cause, and a weighted survival::coxph() is fitted to the expanded data with a robust variance clustered on subject, as the survival::finegray() documentation recommends. Coefficients are log subdistribution hazard ratios. The censoring distribution is estimated on each landmark's complete-case model sample and is not stratified; strata() terms in formula stratify the weighted Cox model only.

Missing covariates and failed fits

Each landmark's model uses the rows with no missing values in the variables of formula; n_eligible and n_model in the results show how many rows that leaves. A landmark is not fitted (status "unestimable") when it has no subjects at risk, no complete cases, no target events in the model sample, or a covariate with a single observed value. A fit that warns (for example about convergence, or a coefficient that may be infinite) gets status "warning", and a fit that errors gets "failed". Neither affects the other landmarks, and one warning at the end lists every landmark that did not fit cleanly. A Fine-Gray model at a landmark with no competing events is still fitted (it then equals the Cox model) with status "warning". If a covariate made by an lme model in add_landmark_covariates() did not fit cleanly at a landmark, that landmark's status is at least "warning" and its message names the covariate.

Interpretation

Each model is conditional on being event-free and under follow-up at its landmark, so different landmarks describe different populations. Fits at different landmarks share subjects and are not independent, so differences between landmarks are not tested. Standard errors treat covariates derived by add_landmark_covariates() as known values; for lme covariates they are therefore too small, because the mixed models were estimated from the same subjects.

See also

tidy.landmark_fit(), landmark_data(), add_landmark_covariates()

Examples

# PBC: status 0 = censored, 1 = transplant, 2 = death
pbc_lm <- pbcseq_baseline |>
  landmark_data(id, futime, status, landmarks = c(365, 730), horizon = 1825) |>
  add_landmark_covariates(pbcseq_visits, id, day, locf = c(bili, albumin))
#> ℹ Ignored 32 rows of `longitudinal_data` whose `id` is not in `landmark_data`.

# Cause-specific Cox model for death (transplant is a competing event)
fit <- fit_landmark(pbc_lm, ~ age + log(bili) + albumin, cause = 2)
fit
#> <landmark_fit> Cause-specific Cox model for cause 2 at 2 landmark(s)
#> Formula: ~age + log(bili) + albumin
#> Horizon: 1825 (relative to each landmark)
#>  landmark n_eligible n_model n_event n_competing fit_status
#>       365        290     290      76          20         ok
#>       730        278     278      76          26         ok
#> 
#> Use tidy() for coefficients and summary() for hazard ratios.
tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 17
#>   .landmark term      estimate std.error statistic  p.value conf.low conf.high
#>       <dbl> <chr>        <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1       365 age          1.05     0.0108      4.49 6.97e- 6    1.03      1.07 
#> 2       365 log(bili)    3.39     0.127       9.60 8.36e-22    2.64      4.35 
#> 3       365 albumin      0.572    0.280      -2.00 4.57e- 2    0.330     0.989
#> 4       730 age          1.05     0.0108      4.81 1.55e- 6    1.03      1.08 
#> 5       730 log(bili)    3.32     0.129       9.30 1.45e-20    2.58      4.27 
#> 6       730 albumin      0.610    0.271      -1.82 6.82e- 2    0.358     1.04 
#> # ℹ 9 more variables: origin <chr>, n_eligible <int>, n_model <int>,
#> #   n_event <int>, n_competing <int>, .model <chr>, .cause <int>,
#> #   .fit_status <chr>, .message <chr>

# Fine-Gray model for death
fit_fg <- fit_landmark(
  pbc_lm, ~ age + log(bili) + albumin, model = "finegray", cause = 2
)
summary(fit_fg)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 17
#>   .landmark term      estimate std.error statistic  p.value conf.low conf.high
#>       <dbl> <chr>        <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1       365 age          1.06     0.0124     4.35  1.33e- 5    1.03       1.08
#> 2       365 log(bili)    3.26     0.113     10.5   8.93e-26    2.62       4.07
#> 3       365 albumin      0.624    0.300     -1.57  1.17e- 1    0.347      1.12
#> 4       730 age          1.06     0.0132     4.71  2.52e- 6    1.04       1.09
#> 5       730 log(bili)    3.03     0.119      9.30  1.45e-20    2.40       3.82
#> 6       730 albumin      0.740    0.308     -0.976 3.29e- 1    0.404      1.35
#> # ℹ 9 more variables: origin <chr>, n_eligible <int>, n_model <int>,
#> #   n_event <int>, n_competing <int>, .model <chr>, .cause <int>,
#> #   .fit_status <chr>, .message <chr>

# The native coxph() fit for one landmark
fit$models[["365"]]
#> Call:
#> survival::coxph(formula = Surv(.time, .status == 2L) ~ age + 
#>     log(bili) + albumin, data = d, model = TRUE)
#> 
#>               coef exp(coef) se(coef)      z        p
#> age        0.04848   1.04968  0.01079  4.495 6.97e-06
#> log(bili)  1.22076   3.38977  0.12722  9.595  < 2e-16
